newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end softer amid currency weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end softer amid currency weakness.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trade on Wednesday, amid a sharp drop in the Canadian dollar and weakness in U.S. treasuries, analysts said.

"The U.S. market being down, our currency tending to be weaker, although the Bank of Canada has been able to stem the tide for now, and the fact that activity levels aren't that high, seems to have helped our market move down," said Dawn Desjardins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.43 to C$116.24 to yield 6.731 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 20/32 to yield 6.74 percent. The spread in yields moved to a negative spread of one basis point from a positive spread of two basis points at Tuesday's close.
The Canadian dollar closed at C$1.3933 (US$0.7172) in moderate trading after the Bank of Canada intervened repeatedly to buy Canadian dollars near the C$1.3960 (US$0.7163).
Traders said the weakness in the currency was prompted by strong broad-based interest to sell Canada dollars through the session.
Canadian bonds were also weaker amid a softer U.S. market. Bonds there traded in a see-saw fashion before ending lower on a late wave of selling despite a successful five-year auction.

Analysts said the Canadian market was looking ahead to the release on Thursday of U.S. jobless claims data for clues on whether the Federal Reserve would hike rates when its Open Market Committe met next week.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.27 to C$108.09 to yield 6.147 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which fell 10/32 to yield 6.45 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 30 basis points from 29 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.88 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.10 percent.
